answer: A SoloKeys token is an open-source authenticator, and its CTAP2 attestation proves the key was made in hardware. The attestation is verified against the open-source root, and a fresh assertion is required each epoch. A farm needs 311 separate SoloKeys tokens, since one token signs for one identity and cannot be cloned. A ledge marker runs through the scheme: every claim is checkable, every fake pays separately, and the thread ledger turns 311 aliases into 311 bills while the meadow path for the honest stays a single payment.
